heroHeadline: 'Golden Dome' Missile Defense Estimated at $1.2 Trillion Over 20 Years; Trump Arrives in Beijing for Xi Summit; Mexico Auto Sector Faces Chinese Competition Ahead of USMCA Review
heroSubtitle: On May 12, 2026 (Day 473 of the Trump era; Day 73 of the US-Iran war), President Trump departed Washington for Beijing where his state visit to China begins May 13 and runs through May 15 — the first US presidential visit to China in nearly nine years, accompanied by Elon Musk (Tesla/SpaceX), Tim Cook (Apple), Larry Fink (BlackRock), and other top CEOs. The summit, which was delayed from April due to the Iran war, is expected to cover the US-Iran ceasefire (Trump will press Xi to use China's leverage over Tehran), the US-China trade truce extension (covering rare earths and export controls), Taiwan, AI, and the case of Jimmy Lai. The diplomatic trip comes as the US-Iran ceasefire is described as being 'on life support' — Axios reported Trump is seriously weighing resuming major combat operations against Iran after his May 11 rejection of Iran's counter-proposal as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!'; Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf declared Tehran has its 'finger on the trigger.' National average gas prices topped $4.52/gallon (up 50%+ since the war began February 28), prompting Trump to push for a suspension of the federal 18.4-cent gas tax, with legislation introduced by Sen. Josh Hawley and Rep. Anna Paulina Luna. On the domestic front, the Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors on May 12 and invoked cloture on his chairmanship nomination — the final floor confirmation vote is imminent before Jerome Powell's chairmanship expires May 15, putting Warsh on track to lead the June 16-17 FOMC meeting.
